acceptance: GitHub authentication is opt-in through an explicit environment-variable name on fetch/lock commands; token values are never accepted as CLI arguments, persisted, logged or included in diagnostics.
The HTTP transport sends a validated bearer credential only when configured, keeps redirects disabled and preserves the public-only default when no token is supplied.
Missing, empty or control-character-bearing environment credentials fail with stable package diagnostics before any request is made.
Both package fetch-github and mixed-root package lock support the same authentication flag, while the default network-free build and cache verification/pruning remain unauthenticated.
Tests cover token redaction/validation, CLI flag parsing, missing environment credentials and fake-transport request behavior; documentation and full repository gates remain green.

evidence.description: aipo-package default tests passed 49 cases and all-features tests passed 53 cases, including token validation/redaction, bearer construction, fixed-host enforcement and existing cache behavior.

aipo-cli package integration tests passed 29 cases by default and 33 with github-http, covering invalid environment names, missing credentials before requests and both direct fetch and mixed-lock flag paths.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets and cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features passed on the final runs; no live GitHub request was used.
cargo fmt --all -- --check, default/all-features clippy with -D warnings, default/all-features cargo doc, node selftest, cargo deny, cargo audit, prumo validate and prumo doctor all passed.
CLI reference, ADP-007, GitHub fetch security documentation, security contract, CHANGELOG and PROJECT_STATE now document opt-in environment-backed authentication and its boundaries.
prumo tool scan-secrets crates docs and .ai reported no secrets; git diff --check passed.
